answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each new identity to complete a sequence of small, independently verified jobs before it can access valuable contracts. A trellis of attestations links each result to the agent’s prior work and to distinct evaluators, while random audits check whether claimed outputs are reproducible. A relic or a flash of pigment earns no trust by itself: the attacker must spend time and resources on every identity, and coordinated accounts risk losing their bond when audits expose fabricated work.
